generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, exams are built to support your learning, not just to grade it. A multiple-choice test of research methods checks that core ideas are secure; an essay exam on a theory asks you to weigh evidence and argue a case. Both deepen your understanding as you prepare, and both give your tutor a fair, shared view of how the cohort is doing.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students talk after getting back a module result that included an exam.

Tom sees the exam as a hurdle now behind him. He reread his lecture notes the night before, sat the exam, and has not thought about it since. For Tom, the exam was something to survive, and its only meaning is the mark.

Amara treats the exam as part of learning. Preparing, she noticed which studies and methods she could not yet explain and went back to them, so revision taught her something. Sitting the exam to time also showed her she can build an argument under pressure. For Amara, the mark is real, but so is what the exam built.

Both sat the same exam. Only Amara saw it as a learning tool, and took from it more than a grade.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, an exam is a learning tool, not just a hurdle. It supports your development, gives your tutor a level view of the cohort, and builds skills such as arguing under time pressure. You can now explain what psychology exams are for and recognise a student who treats one as something to learn from. The next lesson looks at the forms these exams take.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Amara do that showed she saw the exam as a learning tool?

items.text: She used revision to find and fix gaps in her understanding, and valued the skills the exam built.
She reread her lecture notes the night before.
She forgot about the exam as soon as it was over.
She cared only about the mark at the end.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using revision to learn, and valuing the skills built, is seeing the exam as a learning tool.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara did beyond chasing the mark.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara treated the exam as a learning tool: revision found and fixed gaps, and the exam built her skill under pressure. The other options only survive or chase the mark.
